item.title: FCTA upgrades 20 PHCs, says pregnant women to get ambulance in 4 mins
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Capital Territory Administration FCTA has upgraded 20 primary health centres across the territory, declaring that it has cut emergency ambulance response to pregnant women to less than four minutes. Mandate Secretary, FCT Health Services and Environment Secretariat, Dr Adedolapo Fasawe, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja at the community engagement and inauguration of the renovated and upgraded Owner-Occupier Model Primary Health Centre PHC, Kubwa. She said the upgrade was carried out under the World Bank-supported Immunisation Plus and Malaria Progress by Accelerating Coverage and Transforming Services IMPACT project. To demonstrate how the emergency system works, Fasawe asked a pregnant woman to call one of the emergency lines. The ambulance reached the scene in less than four minutes. She said emergency response had been strengthened through the FCT Emergency Medical Services and Ambulance System (FEMSAS), which operates 24 hours a day, is free of charge, and brings local transport operators into the system to convey pregnant women during emergencies. According to her, the intervention goes beyond physical renovation. The administration has also built staff accommodation, provided modern medical equipment and installed solar-powered systems to guarantee 24-hour electricity and round-the-clock service. “The PHC is usually the first port of call for most residents. This is fundamental to improving health outcomes, reducing preventable deaths, and achieving universal health coverage. “This is just one of 20 primary healthcare centres across different communities in the FCT that were upgraded under the IMPACT project,” she added. On affordability, she said at least 1,000 vulnerable residents were being registered free of charge on the spot into the FCT Health Insurance Scheme under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund. The enrolment, she explained, entitles them to one year of free medical care in accredited public and private hospitals. Fasawe also commended the Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, for road construction and rehabilitation projects across the satellite towns, which she said had drastically reduced travel time to health facilities. She said the administration’s healthcare intervention rests on three pillars, which are access, affordability and quality, in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu. Fasawe urged traditional rulers and community leaders to take ownership of the upgraded facilities, monitor service delivery and make sure patients are not charged for free services. “Healthcare should not be a luxury reserved for a few. Quality healthcare is your fundamental human right,” she said. The Executive Secretary of the FCT Primary Health Care Board, Dr Dan Gadzama, said the Federal Government initiative began in 2021 with an initial completion date of December 2025. item.title: Democrats fire starting gun on 2028 White House race
item.description: Democrats fired the starting gun Monday on the race to win back the White House, announcing plans for 12 debates to pick their standard bearer for 2028 as the party looks to build on its sweeping midterm election victory. The first debate is scheduled for June next year, setting the stage for what could be a crowded contest to select a challenger to the Republicans, who must find a successor to term-limited President Donald Trump. The announcement comes as Democrats celebrate their biggest majority in the House of Representatives since the early 1990s, with their victories this month transforming the balance of power in Washington and raising expectations for the next two years. “Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle,” Democratic National Committee chairman Ken Martin said. The party will hold five debates in 2027 and seven in 2028, the final one scheduled for March of that year. The debates will help voters choose the party’s presidential nominee through a series of state-by-state primary elections and caucuses, in which supporters select the candidate they want to face the Republican nominee in November 2028. Under new rules announced Monday, candidates seeking a place on the debate stage must pledge to denounce spending on their behalf by outside political groups, including those that do not disclose their donors. The requirement is intended to curb the influence of wealthy donors and so-called “dark money” in Democratic nomination contests, a longstanding demand of the party’s progressive wing. With a potentially large field, some debates could be spread across two nights, with a maximum of 20 candidates participating. No major Democrat has formally entered the race, but maneuvering is already underway among politicians seeking to become the party’s standard-bearer. Gavin Newsom, Josh Shapiro and Andy Beshear — the governors of California, Pennsylvania and Kentucky, respectively — are among those attracting attention as possible contenders. item.title: 2027 polls: Rigging could push Nigeria into civil war, says Gbenga Hashim
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Dr. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has warned that any attempt to rig the 2027 general election could plunge Nigeria into a civil war. Hashim gave the warning during an interview on Symfoni Podcast, hosted by Olawale Oluwade, at the weekend, where he spoke on the state of the nation, insecurity and the credibility of the electoral process. He said Nigeria was already facing a dangerous combination of insecurity, political mistrust and weaknesses in the electoral system, which could create opportunities for armed non-state actors to exploit any post-election crisis. “The moment there’s a slight political crisis, the militia and terrorist groups, who are well organised, may take advantage of the political instability to expand and declare control in some states in the North and they will begin to press towards Abuja,” he said. The Accord Party candidate also criticised President Bola Tinubu’s handling of national crises, alleging that the President had repeatedly failed to remain in the country and confront challenges directly. “And President Tinubu will do the usual thing he does best, which is to run away. He is always away, he cannot stay to solve any problem; he will run away, he will take a flight out of the country,” Hashim said. He identified allegations that millions of fake names and artificial intelligence-generated photographs had been loaded into the Independent National Electoral Commission’s voters’ register as part of the concerns threatening the credibility of the 2027 elections. Hashim also questioned INEC’s level of preparedness less than two months before the election, while faulting the decision to postpone the clean-up of the voters’ register until after the polls. He warned that conducting the election amid rising insecurity and political violence, coupled with alleged electoral manipulation, could undermine the legitimacy of the government that would emerge from the exercise. “With the current insecurity, political violence and adding election rigging in 2027 will delegitimize the government completely and this could open space for non-state actors, insurgents, etc., already operating in 17 out of the 19 northern states to take advantage of the situation,” he warned. According to him, governors in most of the affected states have lost effective control of some rural communities, with insurgents allegedly imposing taxes on residents in areas under their influence. He said the development demonstrated the organisational capacity and financial resources available to the armed groups, warning that any political instability arising from the 2027 elections could further strengthen their operations. Hashim further cautioned that a disputed election could provide insurgents with an opportunity to expand their territorial influence and advance towards state capitals, potentially escalating the security crisis into a wider conflict. item.title: 2027: INEC warns against ‘rig and die’ slogan, debunks voting without PVC
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has cautioned politicians and their supporters against the use of the inflammatory slogan “rig and die” ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC), Mr Mohammed Haruna, gave the warning on Monday in Abuja, during the commission zonal forum with media stakeholders. Participants of the forum include the leadership of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Nigerian Institute of Social Media Analysts (NISMA), Newspaper Proprietors Association of Nigeria (NPAN), and media executives. Haruna represented by the Deputy Director, Information and Publicity, Wilfred Ifogah, warned that such rhetoric threatened the lives of electoral officials and voters. Speaking on the theme “Ethical and Professional Standards in Election Reporting ahead of 2027 General Election’, he noted that linking electoral offences to death was dangerous and could trigger mob violence at polling units. ”Consider the phrase “rig and die”, now widely repeated. Whatever its originators intend, though some people insist it is aimed only at those who rig, a slogan that links an electoral offence to death is dangerous. ”At the polling unit, the people most exposed are not powerful politicians but ordinary Nigerians serving as presiding officers, assistant presiding officers, collation officers and other ad hoc staff, alongside voters, party agents and observers. ”A charged crowd can easily mistake a delayed result, a technical difficulty or a rumour for rigging, and a mistake of that kind can never be undone. ”Rigging is a crime, and the Electoral Act 2026 prescribes penalties for it. The remedy lies in the law: vigilant observation, transparent results on IReV, formal complaints to the commission and the security agencies, and where necessary, the courts. ”The right to life is guaranteed by Section 33 of the Constitution, and no one may take it on suspicion,’’ he said. He urged political leaders to retire violent rhetoric and appealed to journalists not to amplify threats as headlines or trending hashtags. According to him, threats of violence are not robust political debate. They are offences and the security agencies have a duty to act on them. ”No journalists also should be intimidated for doing their work. A free press and a safe election go together.” The INEC national commissioner and chairman IVEC, also explained that the commission held itself to account, noting that any staff or ad hoc official who compromised an election would face the full weight of the law. ”The Act provides penalties for result manipulation, vote buying and the frustration of upload of polling unit results to the IReV. ”We are also working to have officials and materials at polling units by about 7; 30 a.m., on election day because delays breed suspicion,” he said. He also expressed confidence in Hamzat’s ability to build on the current administration’s achievements to expand economic opportunities and improve living standards in the state. ​In his address at the rally, Hamzat stated that his “PROMISE” agenda was designed to deliver broader democratic dividends if he is elected governor. item.title: Trade Fair leader seeks Lagos support for 5km road
item.description: By Elizabeth Osayande The newly re-elected President of the Balogun Business Association (BBA), Hon. Oscar Paul Ikechukwu Odogwu, has called on the Lagos State Government to partner with the association to rehabilitate the five-kilometre road network within the Trade Fair Complex. Odogwu made the appeal after securing re-election last Tuesday in an exercise whose results were announced by the Chairman of the Electoral Committee, Mr John Nwosu. Speaking on his priorities for the new tenure, he identified poor roads and inadequate parking facilities as major challenges facing the complex, which he described as an international centre for commerce. “The 5km road we have here is in a sorry state. We are trying to get government involved to make sure the roads and drainage are fixed, so that we have free flow of goods and services, trucks and cars moving around in the complex,” he said. He disclosed that his administration was also in discussions with Providus Bank on plans to establish a multi-level car park within the complex. “We don’t have much space inside our complex. What we plan to do is to have a multi-level car park, so our customers and our people will have somewhere to park. But if we can partner with government, that will be fine too,” he said. Odogwu also dismissed reports of tension and crisis surrounding the election, insisting that the exercise was peaceful and credible. “There is no crisis. Not even one person was touched. It is the work of rumour mongers trying to dissuade people from coming out to vote,” he said. He attributed the credibility of the election to the independence of the electoral committee, adding that the committee conducted the exercise without interference. “To the best of my knowledge, it is free and fair. The electoral committee is independent,” he said. On the security arrangements, Odogwu explained that approval had been obtained from the Inspector-General of Police for the conduct of the election. “We are all law-abiding citizens, but when it comes to election time, security must be present because anything can happen,” he said. He said the association adopted a cluster-by-cluster voting system, under which votes were counted in each cluster before being forwarded to the collation centre. On his re-election, Odogwu said his administration would build on the achievements of its first tenure and intensify efforts to address the challenges facing traders and businesses in the complex. “In our first tenure, by the grace of God, we delivered a lot of projects. Now that we have been voted back, we are going to do more,” he said. The Chairman of the Lagos Cluster, Chief Christopher Lucas, and a voter, Mrs Patricia Umenze, also described the election as peaceful. item.title: Trump says Nvidia’s reinstatement of Huang ‘correct and proper decision’
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Monday hailed AI giant Nvidia’s decision to bring back co-founder Jensen Huang less than two weeks after he resigned over an alleged spy scandal. In a Truth Social post Trump, who has been calling for Huang to be brought back, also said the US government “has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.” “The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump wrote. He added: “the Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” He called Huang “a Great Patriot.” Trump said Nvidia should press on with an internal investigation into its compliance with US rules designed to keep China from obtaining the company’s most advanced chips for training and running AI models. In separate remarks Monday to a PBS reporter, Trump declined to comment on a New York Times report that the alleged spy at the heart of the scandal was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during the affair with Huang. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent insisted Sunday the administration needs to know more about Nvidia’s sales abroad of its top-line chips. item.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior US government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.” The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead,” the company said in a statement. Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board. The decision came three days after Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.” Trump described Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions,” and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart.” Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused. Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.” Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips. US intelligence services reportedly concluded she passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations. Board chair Harvey Jones said Monday that directors now believe Huang “is the right person to lead Nvidia” and that his return serves the interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers. Jones, a former Synopsys chief executive who was named Nvidia’s first-ever board chair during the crisis, will stay in the role. Chief financial officer Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, will continue as CFO. Nvidia said a committee of independent directors set up earlier this month to investigate whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort will see its probe through to the end. Huang supports the investigation and has committed to cooperating, the company said. Vanguard News The post Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Eurozone business activity still growing despite French downturn
item.description: Business activity in the euro area registered a “steady” expansion this month, a key survey showed Monday, as faster growth in Germany helped counter a deepening downturn in France. The eurozone purchasing managers’ index (PMI) published by S&P Global, a gauge of the economy’s overall health, stood at 51.7 in November, unchanged from October, but below the 52.0 forecast of economists surveyed by FactSet. A reading above 50 indicates growth while one below 50 signals contraction. “At the headline level, the flash PMI data signal sustained steady growth for the eurozone in November, consistent with the economy growing at a near 0.3 percent pace in the fourth quarter,” S&P chief business economist Chris Williamson said in a statement. But he cautioned that the “overall picture of continuing economic resilience masks worrying divergences in performance within the euro area.” “While growth in Germany has accelerated to the fastest for four and a half years, as its manufacturing sector enjoys a growth spurt of the likes not seen for over five years, France is suffering a deepening downturn,” Williamson said. The German economy, he said, was benefiting strongly from “surging investment spending on defence and AI-related technologies”. At the same time, “uncertainty about the political environment, social unrest and the high cost of living are hitting service providers especially hard, especially for consumer-facing businesses, dampening growth both in France and across the rest of the region as a whole”. The European Central Bank has lifted borrowing costs twice this year in response to the energy shock triggered by the US war on Iran, and Williamson warned that “higher interest rates are also starting to show up as an increasing drag”. He noted that lower oil prices had “helped tame inflationary pressures” somewhat in November. But he predicted the PMI data alongside a “broad message” of eurozone growth would bolster calls for a further rate increase in December. item.title: Murray-Bruce hails Tinubu’s CNG bus initiative, urges governors to act
item.description: Former Senator Ben Murray-Bruce has commended President Bola Tinubu’s initiative to introduce compressed natural gas (CNG)-powered buses and promote local vehicle assembly, urging state governors to invest in the programme and supporting infrastructure. Murray-Bruce, founder of Silverbird Group, made the call in a Facebook post on Monday, describing the initiative as a step towards transforming Nigeria from a consumer nation into a producer economy. He welcomed the Federal Government’s partnership with Chinese automobile manufacturer Yutong to supply 100 CNG buses to Lagos State by December, followed by plans for local assembly in Ibadan, Oyo State. According to the former lawmaker, local assembly of the buses would create employment and ensure that more economic benefits remain within the country. “Every bus we assemble at home is a salary paid at home,” he said. Murray-Bruce also highlighted the impact of CNG-powered public transportation on commuters, citing a reduction in transport fares on the Enugu-Nsukka route from N4,000 to N1,600. He said the reduction would provide relief for students, traders, healthcare workers and other commuters struggling with transportation costs. “The numbers already speak. On the Enugu to Nsukka route, the fare has fallen from N4,000 to N1,600. For a student, a trader, or a nurse, that is not a statistic. That is dinner,” he said. The former senator urged state governors to take advantage of the Federal Government’s initiative by procuring CNG buses, investing in refuelling infrastructure and addressing long queues at existing CNG stations. “Now, my dear governors, the President has opened the door. Walk through it. Buy the buses, build the refuelling stations, and end the long CNG queues before they become the new fuel queues,” he said. He argued that the success of the country’s economic reforms should be measured by their impact on the daily lives of Nigerians, particularly through reduced transportation costs. “Reform is not a speech. Reform is a cheaper ride to work,” Murray-Bruce added. The post Murray-Bruce hails Tinubu’s CNG bus initiative, urges governors to act appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: France Detains Three Over Mystery Train Accident
item.description: French police on Monday arrested three people at a traveller camp in connection with the September derailment of a train that injured 44 people, two sources with knowledge of the matter said. In France, the term “travellers” refers to communities who maintain an itinerant lifestyle, including some of Romani origin. The train, carrying 186 passengers, derailed on September 11 between the cities of Rouen and Caen in Normandy, northwestern France. Railway workers work on the removal of a derailed train carriage in Cleon, northwestern France, on September 16, 2026. Photo by GUILLAUME SALIGOT / AFP Prosecutors at the time said the driver had tested negative for alcohol or drugs and that a section of rail found on the track may have caused the derailment. A local official said the fragment weighed around 300 kilograms. Police on Monday detained a 45-year-old and his 22-year-old twin sons at the camp near the site of the accident, one of the sources told AFP. They were taken into police custody on suspicion of attempted theft, theft committed by a group, and involuntary bodily injury, the source said. After the derailment, President Emmanuel Macron warned of the growing threat posed by Moscow’s shadow operations across Europe, saying he had ordered measures to protect France’s critical infrastructure. item.title: War: Iran Seeks $290bn In Damages Against US
item.description: Iranian courts have demanded that the United States pay $290 billion in damages, a judiciary official said on Monday. “We have secured court rulings in domestic courts awarding $290 billion in damages against the Americans,” said Hassan Abdolianpour, head of the judiciary’s centre for lawyers, according to state television. He also said that several lawsuits have been filed against the Gulf Arab nations for “allowing their territory to be used by America to launch attacks against Iran”. According to state TV, the damages cover US actions going back decades. File photo showing US-Iran flags. The Middle East war began on February 28 when the United States and Israel launched a wave of strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, saying it is targeting US-Israeli bases and assets in those countries. The Islamabad memorandum of understanding signed in June between the US and Iran, which aimed to pave the way to a peace deal, included a clause that would see Washington and its regional partners drawing up a plan with at least $300 billion “for the reconstruction and economic development” of Iran. Moreover, Iran has been under crippling sanctions by the United States for decades, mainly over its nuclear program. item.title: Scramble To Save Climate Fight After COP Collapse
item.description: Officials voiced dismay on Monday at the collapse of UN climate talks, urging the world not to abandon joint efforts to curb the deadly warming of the planet. A final agreement was rejected on Sunday at the COP31 climate summit, with delegates failing to strike an agreement over fossil fuels amid resistance from oil-producing countries. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres voiced “profound frustration” while key player China expressed disappointment — but insisted the green transition was “irreversible”. COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (C) attends a plenary session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Centre, in Antalya on November 22, 2026. The EU issued a plea to salvage multilateral efforts to fight climate change, which is worsening the risk and impact of deadly storms, floods and droughts. “It is absolutely crucial that the multilateral process stays alive,” said European Commission spokeswoman Anna-Kaisa Itkonen, calling the talks’ failure a “terrible outcome”. Familiar fault lines emerged at COP31 over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas. Oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal at the conference co-hosted by Turkey and Australia. Negotiations chair Chris Bowen who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”. Geopolitical worries Australian Minister for Climate Change and Energy and President of COP31 Negotiations Chris Bowen (C) and COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (3rd R) and delegates before a session during the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center, in Antalya, on November 22, 2026. Photo by YASIN AKGUL / AFP Bowen, Australia’s climate minister, said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”, as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity. Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from heatwaves in Europe to floods in Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis. item.title: Woman arrested for assaulting policeman in Abia
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Abia State Police Command has arrested a woman, identified as Ettoh Barkerk, for allegedly assaulting a police inspector and tearing his uniform during an operation in Aba. The suspect was arrested after police officers from the Ndiegoro Division responded to a distress call reporting that hoodlums were attacking members of the congregation at Christ the King Catholic Church (CKC), Aba. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Maureen Chinaka, who confirmed the incident, said the suspect allegedly became violent when officers arrived at the scene, assaulted one of them and attempted to retrieve recovered exhibits. According to Chinaka, the incident occurred on November 22, 2026, when the division received information that some hoodlums were throwing fireworks indiscriminately within the church premises, causing panic and threatening public peace. She said a patrol team was immediately deployed to the area to contain the situation, prevent further escalation and restore order. “Upon receipt of the report, a patrol team from the Division swiftly mobilised to the scene to contain the situation, prevent further escalation and restore public order. In the course of the operation, one Ettoh Barkerk (female) was apprehended at the scene with fireworks in her possession. “However, the suspect became violent and physically assaulted an Inspector attached to the patrol team, tore his uniform and attempted to forcibly retrieve the recovered exhibits. “The suspect was subsequently subdued and arrested, while the recovered fireworks and other relevant exhibits were secured for investigation. She will be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigation,” she said. The police spokesperson said the command condemned the alleged assault, describing it as unacceptable conduct that fell short of the standards of civility and respect for the law. She added that normalcy had been restored within the church premises, while security monitoring had been intensified in the area to prevent further breaches of public peace. item.title: England launches world’s largest AI-aided breast cancer screening trial
item.description: England’s state-run health service said Monday it has launched the world’s largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, which is set to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years. The National Health Service (NHS) hailed the new trial as having the potential to transform breast cancer diagnosis, as it announced hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset. The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess if tools assisted by artificial intelligence can help improve early cancer detection in screening, which health officials hope will then free up specialist clinicians’ time. The AI-assisted reading tool will assist clinicians in reviewing images collected from routine mammograms, according to the NHS. “This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world,” Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement, lauding the tech’s “huge potential” while pledging “proper safeguards” to ensure safety and effectiveness. “If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery.” The trial is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working closely with NHS England. Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out. The NHS stressed screening appointments will proceed as normal, but the AI-assisted tool will be used alongside specialists checking the images to look for cancers that are too small to see or feel. The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two. Recruitment has started at Cambridge University Hospitals, in eastern England, with more of the 30 selected sites opening in the coming months. Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women, with around 55,000 diagnosed every year in the UK. Women aged 50 to 71 are invited for screening every three years, amounting to around 2.1 million screenings annually. The NHS estimates this helps prevent around 1,300 deaths. A study published in The Lancet medical journal in January said that AI can improve breast cancer detection through more effective screening while reducing radiologists’ workloads. It analysed nearly 106,000 mammograms performed in Sweden as part of its national breast cancer screening programme — involving women with a median age of 53 — from April 2021 to early December 2022. item.title: Shettima tasks stakeholders on implementation of drug control plan
item.description: ….AGF, Marwa say new NDCMP will strengthen NDLEA; ECOWAS, Reps commend initiative By Kingsley Omonobi Vice-President Kashim Shettima has urged federal and state governments, the National Assembly, private sector operators and other stakeholders to ensure the effective implementation of the National Drug Control Master Plan (NDCMP) 2026–2030. Shettima said the five-year plan must be implemented with urgency, discipline and accountability, stressing that drug control should remain a national priority. The Vice-President spoke on Monday in Abuja as Special Guest of Honour at the official launch of the plan, which he commended to all institutions and stakeholders on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. Represented by the Special Adviser to the President on Special Duties, Office of the Vice-President, Dr Modibbo Aliyu Umar, Shettima said Nigeria could not secure its future without protecting the people responsible for building it. He described drug abuse and trafficking as public health concerns, security threats, development challenges and economic issues, warning that enforcement alone would not address the problem without prevention, treatment and measures to tackle illicit financial flows sustaining drug markets. “Our response must therefore be comprehensive, coordinated and sustained,” he said. Shettima identified the six pillars of the new plan as Supply Reduction; Drug Demand Reduction; Access to Controlled Medicines for Scientific and Medical Purposes; Alternative Development and Sustainable Livelihoods; Disruption of the Illicit Drug Economy; and Governance, Financing and Coordination. He commended the leadership of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), under Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), for making Nigeria the first African country to commence an Alternative Development programme, whose pilot project is being implemented in three communities in Ondo State. He urged state and local governments to embrace the initiative and take ownership of its implementation. On funding, the Vice-President warned that a national policy without a credible financing framework risked becoming a mere declaration of good intentions. He, therefore, directed that the plan’s priorities be incorporated into institutional work plans, budget proposals and implementation schedules. He challenged stakeholders to identify immediate actions their respective institutions must take to ensure the success of the initiative, insisting that global challenges should not become an excuse for inaction. “Five years from now, the significance of today’s launch will not be judged by the ceremony,” he said. “Let this be the moment Nigeria moves from policy to action.” In his welcome address, NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Marwa, said the new master plan was designed to consolidate previous achievements, address identified shortcomings and respond to emerging drug-related threats. item.title: Military air strikes kill 37 terrorists, destroy four vehicles
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian military says it has neutralised 37 terrorists and destroyed four vehicles in a series of precision air strikes conducted across the North-East between November 16 and 23, 2026. The operations, carried out by the Air Component of Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), also led to the destruction of a terrorist staging facility and disrupted suspected improvised explosive device (IED) activities along troops’ operational routes. Acting Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force (North-East), Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni, disclosed this on Monday, saying the air component conducted six precision strikes across five locations within the theatre during the period. He said the operations, supported by credible intelligence and persistent Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR), targeted terrorist movements, hideouts and logistics assets in Monguno Local Government Area, Kerenoa and Fage in Marte LGA, and the Tumbuma Baba general area of Kukawa LGA, Borno State. According to him, a pre-emptive air strike was conducted following intelligence gathering, with subsequent Battle Damage Assessment (BDA) confirming that 10 terrorists were neutralised, while several others sustained injuries. Goni said that in a separate operation on November 17, ISR surveillance identified a terrorist staging facility at Arina Chiki, where insurgents were reportedly planning an attack on troops’ defensive positions. He said the location was engaged with precision fire, with subsequent assessment confirming the destruction of the targeted building and no further movement observed within the structure. Similarly, on November 20, military surveillance assets identified two terrorist vehicles concealed near a tree in Kerenoa. The vehicles were engaged and destroyed in a precision air strike. On the same day, another terrorist vehicle was identified at a suspected IED assembly location in the Fage general area, where insurgents were reportedly preparing to plant explosives along a route used by troops. The vehicle was immediately engaged and destroyed, disrupting the suspected IED-related activity. Goni said further successes were recorded on November 23 in the Tumbuma Baba general area of Kukawa LGA, where an intelligence-led operation identified and destroyed another terrorist vehicle. During the operation, two suspected terrorists were observed emerging from a nearby life-support structure. He said persistent ISR subsequently tracked the suspects to a gathering of six other terrorists taking cover under a tree. After additional terrorists joined the group, a precision air strike was launched against the identified position. The subsequent BDA confirmed that all eight terrorists were neutralised, with no further movement observed at the location. item.title: Boat Mishap: Bayelsa Govt To Commission Marine Taskforce In Search Of Missing Persons
item.description: Governor of Bayelsa State, Douye Diri, is set to commission a marine taskforce to intensify the search for victims of a boat mishap that has claimed over 29 lives in the state. The state’s Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Dr. Faith Godwin, who was a guest on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Monday, disclosed that the state government will commission a Safety Marine Taskforce this week as part of the effort to ensure compliance with water transportation safety rules across 30 jetties in Bayelsa State. The development followed Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, with a death toll of 29 recorded so far and over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. She noted that the collaborative effort to recover more bodies as the search continues. “Actually, the effort is still ongoing. The state government is represented by the Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy by Alsace State in collaboration with the State Emergency Management Agency, as well as Nigerian Police, Nigerian Navy, Security Agency, Civil Defence and the Community Rescue Team, the Ministry Rescue Team also. The efforts are still ongoing to see how we can recover more bodies.” Bayelsa State Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Dr. Faith Zibs Godwin speaking on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Monday, November 22, 2026. On why the operator boat which capsized may have flouted safety rules such as overloading, she said, “According to the Maritime Workers Union, as well as the other team who had been at the unit, they said they had to stay clear because the operator at that time felt they didn’t have the right to talk to him. So the boat in question was privately engaged to move persons from that particular location” According to her, the taskforce, which constitutes several government agencies, was set up before the boat incident occurred but will be commissioned this week to ensure safer waterways across the state. “The state government has also constituted, before now, a Marine Safety Task Force, which has to do with coming together of relevant agencies, the National Inland Waterways Representative, that of the Nigerian Navy, the Marine Police Representative and Community Representative to see how they could enforce marine safety measures in our various jetties” She stressed that the task force is empowered to enforce marine safety measures across waterways in the state. ‘The task force has so much to do because it’s an all-inclusive task force in the sense that we have the marine police there, and where operators don’t comply, they would face the law. And our legislative arm too, they are also ready to enact or legislate on certain, you know, state-based policy and laws that we would send to them very soon. So the whole idea is to ensure that what has happened does not repeat itself again.” She added that the Marine taskforce will also be responsible for enforcing boat riverworthiness to ensure safety for passengers. “

item.title: Alice Huang Had Contact With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Boss Affair — Reports
item.description: Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the center of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant’s former chief executive Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday. Alice Huang was this month outed as a suspected Chinese spy, accused of having an affair with Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing. She was in contact with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the intelligence. Alice Huang, who is no relation to Jensen, previously led Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based tech group under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia chips, possibly in violation of US export controls. Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang arrives ahead of a state banquet for US President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People Beijing on May 14, 2026. (Photo by BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI / AFP) According to the Times, Alice Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency correspond to the affair as well as a period when Megaspeed was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips. The Times also reported that US intelligence agencies have gathered evidence that Alice Huang’s business partner Kang Wei — who the newspaper said was often introduced as her husband — worked with the same Chinese spy agency. Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s chief executive earlier this month, following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang. He is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns. The upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia which is at the center of an AI boom that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe. item.description: The Emir of Daura, His Royal Highness Alhaji Faruq Umar-Faruk, has been embroiled in an alleged sexual assault of a foreign tourist who visited his palace in Daura, Katsina State, during her tour of Nigeria. The tourist, who identified herself on Instagram as @beduinqa, alleged in a viral video that the 92-year-old monarch fondled her hand and other body parts. The video has elicited reactions, with Amnesty International Nigeria and prominent voices in the North calling for a thorough probe into the act. When contacted, the Daura Emirate spokesperson (Sarkin Labarai), Ibrahim Murtala, confirmed that the Emirate has seen the video and they are currently analyzing its content, adding that the Emirate will address the matter after the conclusion of the ongoing processes. He did not respond to a text message sent to him either.
